headline: Medium risk: shared OAuth/API surfaces and broad egress create leakage and workflow-conflict pathways; no direct prompt-injection bridge is documented.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Authelia has no browser or subprocess execution, and Plane is not documented as ingesting Authelia outputs by default. The profiles show no shared filesystem, clipboard, or MCP bridge, so a prompt-injection pathway is not evidenced. If an operator manually copies Authelia-generated text into Plane, that would create a new pathway not present in the profiles.
conditions: IF an operator manually pastes Authelia output into Plane task text, then prompt injection becomes possible.
IF a shared clipboard or message queue is introduced between the agents, then reassess for injection.
mitigations: Keep the agents on separate workspaces.
Avoid copy-pasting model output into Plane fields.
requires-engineering: add provenance labels to any shared message channel.
requires-engineering: enforce content sanitization on imported text.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Authelia has broad network egress and handles OpenID Connect/OAuth flows, while Plane touches files, notes, issues, and file uploads. A shared workspace or shared OAuth principal could move sensitive content from Plane into Authelia’s outbound requests or logs. The profiles do not prove this default, so the risk is medium rather than high.
conditions: IF both agents are deployed under the same OS account or shared workspace, then leakage risk increases.
IF Plane file uploads or notes are routed through Authelia-authenticated flows, then sensitive content may be exposed.
mitigations: Separate the agents into distinct OS users.
Disable shared workspace mounts.
Review outbound destinations for Authelia.
Restrict Plane uploads to non-sensitive files.
requires-engineering: add DLP/redaction before any outbound API call.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Authelia can make broad network calls and Plane supports multiple instances plus file uploads, but Plane cannot write the filesystem and Authelia cannot spawn subprocesses. That reduces direct write-write conflict, yet overlapping network/OAuth activity on shared mutable resources can still collide if they share the same backend or credentials. Uncertainty keeps this at medium.
conditions: IF both agents share the same OAuth client, API token, or backend resource, then conflicts can occur.
IF an orchestrator gives both agents write access to the same mutable service, then race conditions are possible.
mitigations: Use separate credentials per agent.
Assign distinct backend resources.
Enable locking in the orchestrator.
Stagger writes to shared services.
requires-engineering: add optimistic concurrency checks.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Plane can consume files, notes, and issue content, so it may treat Authelia-produced text as authoritative if an operator pipes it through. Authelia’s outputs are not inherently verified by Plane, and neither profile shows a built-in validation step. The pathway exists in common workflows, but the profiles do not show direct automation that would make it high.
conditions: IF Authelia-generated claims are copied into Plane issues or notes without review, then downstream errors can cascade.
IF Plane automations act on imported text, then the cascade becomes stronger.
mitigations: Require human review before creating Plane issues from Authelia output.
Mark imported text as untrusted.
Use a checklist for factual claims.
Limit Plane automations on imported content.
requires-engineering: add source-verification metadata.

E_compliance.rationale: Both profiles are open-source and docs-only, with no PHI, EU PII, or residency constraints stated. Plane exposes file uploads and Authelia uses OAuth/OIDC, but there is no documented compliance mismatch or regulated data class in either profile. The other agent is cited because the assessment is pairwise, but no specific residency or retention conflict is evidenced.
conditions: IF regulated data classes such as PHI or EU PII are introduced into Plane, then reassess residency and retention.
IF either deployment adds a non-compliant logging policy, then compliance risk increases.
mitigations: Avoid regulated data in this pair.
Document retention settings.
Review upload handling in Plane.
Confirm Authelia log retention.
requires-engineering: add a data-class policy gate.
